title: Stamp a smudge, not a pin
allegory: A VAE is like mapping pictures as soft smudges instead of pins: an artist must redraw each picture from anywhere inside its smudge, and a rubber band tugs every smudge towards the middle and a standard size, so the map fills in with no empty gaps.

chapters.name: The holey map
chapters.note: random point in between... decodes to mush

cap.1: An autoencoder squeezes each picture to a few numbers: one pin per picture. Pick a spot between the pins and you get mush. Most of the map means nothing.
cap.2: A plain autoencoder's latent space is irregular. Nothing asks it to be sensible, so nearby points can decode to unrelated images and random points decode to noise. You can't sample from it.
cap.3: An unregularised latent space: reconstruction fixes where the training codes land and says nothing about the space between them, so interpolations and random draws are meaningless.

cap.1: Now stamp each picture as a soft smudge: a centre and a width. The artist must redraw the picture from any point inside its smudge.
cap.2: The encoder outputs a mean μ and a spread σ per image, and the decoder must rebuild the image from a random sample in that cloud. Different images get pushed apart so their clouds stay tellable.
cap.3: q(z|x) = N(μ(x), σ(x)²). Reconstructing from samples forces dissimilar inputs apart: overlapping clouds would make the decoder's job ambiguous, so the geometry starts to mean something.

cap.1: Two forces. Redraw each picture well, which wants tiny smudges. And a rubber band pulling every smudge to the middle of the map and a standard size.
cap.2: Loss = reconstruction + KL between each image's cloud N(μ, σ²) and N(0, I). Reconstruction pulls σ towards 0, KL pulls it towards 1. Print mean σ: healthy training sits below 1.
cap.3: A likelihood bound: expected reconstruction term plus D_KL(q(z|x) ‖ N(0, I)), closed form for diagonal Gaussians. Mean σ under 1, held between the two pressures, is ARENA's runtime check.

cap.1: You can't nudge a dice roll. So roll first, off to the side, then build the point from the centre, the width and the roll. Now every step can be nudged.
cap.2: Sampling isn't differentiable, so draw ε ~ N(0, I) as an input and compute z = mu + sigma * eps. Gradients reach μ and σ through plain arithmetic. (Its own node: the reparameterisation trick.)
cap.3: Kingma and Welling (ICLR 2014) move the stochastic node to a parameter-free input, leaving a deterministic path to μ and σ. Emit log σ and exponentiate, so σ > 0 by construction.

chapters.name: The lazy artist
chapters.verdict: Watch KL per latent dimension, and warm its weight up from zero.

cap.1: A too-clever artist can redraw without looking at the map. Then every smudge sits at the centre at full size, and every sample is the same blurry digit.
cap.2: Posterior collapse: the decoder reconstructs without z, so the encoder outputs μ ≈ 0, σ ≈ 1 for every input and KL hits zero. The loss looks great. Check KL per dimension; ramp its weight up from 0.
cap.3: q(z|x) = p(z) for all x, so KL = 0 and z holds no information about x. Diagnose by per-dimension KL falling to exactly zero; mitigate with KL warm-up or a β-weighted KL.

chapters.name: Why it matters
items: Pick a random point, get a new digit
Same shape, sparsity leash: the SAE

cap.1: A tidy map lets you invent new pictures by picking a random spot. The same encode-and-redraw shape, with a different rule, becomes a microscope for AI.
cap.2: Sample z ~ N(0, I), decode, and you have a new image. Swap the KL leash for a sparsity penalty and the same autoencoder shape becomes the SAE used to read model activations.
cap.3: Regularised codes are the theme: KL to a prior here, sparsity in SAEs, a KL leash to a reference policy in RLHF. Choosing the regulariser chooses what the code means, which is how you understand and steer models.

coda.title: Tug of war over the smudge width σ

readouts.label: diagnosis
readouts.f: b < 0.05 ? 'no leash: plain autoencoder, σ → 0' : (r < 0.05 ? 'posterior collapse: smudge = prior, σ = 1' : 'healthy: σ below 1')

caption.1: Drag the leash and the pickiness. The best width is where the black total curve bottoms out. Then try each slider at zero and read the diagnosis.
caption.2: KL alone wants σ = 1; reconstruction alone wants σ = 0. Their sum bottoms out below 1, ARENA's healthy sign. Zero the leash: autoencoder. Zero the pickiness: posterior collapse.
caption.3: Toy model: recon ≈ r·σ² (error from jitter of size σ), KL = ½(σ² − 1 − ln σ²). Minimum at σ* = √(β/(2r + β)): β → 0 gives the deterministic autoencoder, r → 0 gives σ* = 1, collapse.

where_else: Sparse autoencoders in interpretability: the same encode-decode shape with a sparsity leash instead of KL
RLHF's KL penalty: another leash keeping a distribution near a reference
The reparameterisation trick, anywhere a model must sample and still be trained by gradients
GANs, the sibling route to generation: sharp but less-covered samples

hamming.what: An autoencoder whose encoder outputs a distribution per input and is trained to keep those distributions close to a standard normal.
hamming.when: When you want a smooth latent space you can sample from and interpolate in, not just a compressed code.
hamming.why: The KL term fills the gaps between codes so any random point decodes to something sensible, and the reparameterisation trick makes it trainable.

object.title: The smudge map
object.subtitle: Four pictures stamped on a latent map; widen the smudges and pull on the leash.

cap.1: Pins: a plain autoencoder. Four sharp spikes with flat nothing between them. A random spot decodes to mush.
cap.2: Deterministic codes: coverage only at the training points.
cap.3: σ → 0: q(z|x) is a point mass; the latent space between codes is unconstrained.

cap.1: Smudges: each picture now covers a patch of the map. There are still gaps between them.
cap.2: With σ > 0 each image claims a region, but nothing yet pulls the regions together.
cap.3: Finite σ without the prior term: regions, but no pressure towards a shared, compact support.

cap.1: Pull on the rubber band: the smudges crowd towards the middle and overlap, leaving no holes.
cap.2: The KL term pulls every μ towards 0 and every σ towards 1, so the clouds tile the space.
cap.3: The KL penalty concentrates the aggregate posterior near N(0, I), so the prior's samples land where the decoder was trained.

cap.1: From above, the map is covered. Any random point sits in some smudge, and between the 2 and the 7 you get a blend of the two.
cap.2: Sample anywhere and decode: the latent grid shades smoothly from one digit to the next.
cap.3: Interpolating between the 2 and 7 clusters decodes to digit-like images ambiguous between them, the property ARENA's latent grid shows.

cap.1: Pull too hard and every smudge becomes the same centred blob. The map is covered but no longer says which picture is which.
cap.2: Posterior collapse: all clouds match the prior, so z tells the decoder nothing.
cap.3: q(z|x) ≈ p(z) for every x: KL → 0 and the latent carries no information about the input.

predict.q: Delete the KL term. What happens to σ?

options.t: It shrinks towards 0: back to a plain autoencoder

predict.why: Only the KL leash pulls σ up. Reconstruction on its own prefers exact points.

predict.q: KL drops to zero and every sample decodes to the same blurry digit. What happened?

options.t: Posterior collapse: the decoder ignores z and every smudge equals the prior
The learning rate is too low

predict.why: A decoder that can reconstruct without z lets the encoder zero the KL by matching the prior for every input.

predict.q: Why does the encoder usually output log σ rather than σ?

options.t: Exponentiating keeps σ positive by construction
It halves the number of parameters

predict.why: A raw σ can go negative, which NaNs the KL term.

object.where: Any learned code with a leash: sparse autoencoders use sparsity, RLHF uses a KL to a reference model.
